title: Tune two coupled adjusters to the peak of a meter in a few readings
context: Aligning and calibrating coupled adjusters by taking a few costly measurements and inferring where the optimum lies (mirror and antenna mounts, sensors, test fixtures) is a routine step in building and bringing up research hardware. A robot that can do it with a limited measurement budget, instead of exhaustive search, can run such setup and troubleshooting loops unattended and so speed up experiments.
instruction: Press the white READ button between the two tracks to show the red needle for the current positions of the orange (left) and teal (right) sliders; use at most eight READ presses, including at least three at slider positions 10 mm or more apart. Then set both sliders so the needle stands on the green band at the end of the scale, and let go.
setup: All positions are cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (x forward, y left); the table top is z = 0. Base plate: 30.0 x 20.0 x 1.0 cm dark grey, 5.0 kg, centre (30.0, 0.0, 0.5), friction 1.0, fixed. Two parallel tracks at y = +6.0 (left, orange knob) and y = -6.0 (right, teal knob), each 14.0 cm long from x = 17.0 to 31.0: dark-grey side walls 0.6 cm thick and 2.0 cm tall, 0.5 cm end-stop walls at both ends (inner length 13.0 cm), inner width 3.6 cm, 0.2 cm floor made of 2.0 cm position bands that alternate light grey and blue from the near stop (arm side) outward (0-2 blue, 2-4 light, ... 8-10 blue), then grey. Knobs: 3.0 x 3.0 x 1.4 cm, 80 g, friction 0.5, orange (left track) and teal (right track), resting on the floor with 0.3 cm play per side; each starts with its rear face 3.0 cm from the inner face of the near end stop (centre x = 22.0). READ button: a pocket ring 4.8 x 4.8 x 1.6 cm (0.3 cm walls, dark grey, fixed) centred at (33.5, 0.0) holding a white cap 4.0 x 4.0 x 1.2 cm, 20 g, spring 100 N/m, travel 0.8 cm to a hard stop; cap top rests 3.4 cm above the table. Meter housing 4.0 x 20.0 x 3.0 cm dark grey centred at (40.0, 0.0), carrying a white scale bar 16.0 cm long (y = -8.0 to +8.0, 0 mark at y = -8.0), 2.4 cm wide, 0.4 cm thick, with a green band 3.6 cm wide over its last 0.8 cm (y = 7.2 to 8.0), and a bright-red needle 3.4 x 1.2 x 0.8 cm, 10 g, resting at the 0 mark.
scoring: Setting of a knob = distance in mm from the inner face of the near end stop to the knob's rear (arm-side) face; x = left knob, y = right knob, both start at 30. Reading r = exp(-(u^2/(2*45^2) + v^2/(2*9^2))), u = ((x-x0)+(y-y0))/sqrt(2), v = (-(x-x0)+(y-y0))/sqrt(2), peak (x0,y0) = (80,50) mm (hidden variants 1 and 2: (88,72), (95,55)); r >= 0.95 means both knobs within about 4 mm of the peak, or 2 mm if they err in opposite directions. READ registers when the cap is pressed 6.4 mm and re-arms below 1.6 mm; it then shows the needle at 160*r mm from the 0 mark until the next press (the 0.95 mark is the green band's edge). Presses beyond 8 move the needle but do not count. Score at the end, from the knobs' final positions: 0.25 if any knob moved >= 3 mm or READ was pressed; 0.50 if r >= 0.50; 0.75 if r >= 0.80, at most 8 presses in total and >= 2 separated counted presses; 1.0 if r >= 0.95, at most 8 presses, >= 3 separated counted presses, both grippers open, both knobs moving <= 5 mm/s, for 20 consecutive control steps (1.0 s). Separated = at least 10 mm from every earlier separated press in max(|dx|,|dy|). Score 0 for the whole run if a knob leaves its channel (centre > 1.0 cm off the track line or > 4.5 cm above the table) or the base plate moves > 5 mm.
reset_notes: Push both knobs back to 30 mm (rear face 3.0 cm from the near end stop's inner face) with a ruler; they stay where left. Check that the cap springs back to 3.4 cm above the table and that the base plate has not moved. Reset the meter (press counter to 0, needle to the 0 mark) and set the peak switch to position 0 (peak (80, 50) mm). Only the first press that reaches 6.4 mm counts; do not press READ while resetting.
fidelity: Knobs are blocks pushed along U-channels by friction (Coulomb 0.5, no springs). The READ cap is a 100 N/m spring with a hard stop and 20 Hz hysteresis; it is softer than a real switch so the simulated arm can press it. The needle is moved by code to 160*r mm and the hidden r(x, y) is computed in code from the knob positions: there is no physical meter. Real build: same blocks, ring and cap; an electronic meter.
